ui.m5c3408ac8e8d: Tell a story about your weekend in the past tense, then tell it again as if it were happening right now. Switching deliberately makes the tenses stick.
ui.m0753ea304a05: Practice describing what other people do — 'he works', 'she takes', 'they run'. Third-person singular is where the -s goes missing most.
ui.mf9211f7088b3: Describe the room you're in out loud, naming every object with 'a' or 'the'. Ask yourself each time: does the listener already know which one I mean?
ui.mbe0390a5ec8b: Prepositions rarely follow rules — they come in fixed pairs. Collect the ones you get wrong as whole phrases ('depend ON', 'arrive AT') and reuse them in conversation rather than memorising them.
ui.m6366c29484ea: Practice with the awkward uncountables — advice, information, furniture, news, research. Say 'a piece of advice' until 'an advice' starts to sound wrong.
ui.mbfe762d273c0: English holds subject-verb-object hard. Practice placing adverbs — 'he is always late', not 'always he is late' — since that's where word order usually slips.
ui.m6b7471181bb6: Ask Ahmad five questions in a row on purpose. Questions invert the subject and auxiliary, and that inversion is easy to skip when you're speaking fast.
ui.mb4b62110282e: Watch for the dropped subject — English needs one even when it means nothing ('it is raining'). Many languages don't, so this transfers straight across.
ui.m1377a0c68032: A modal is always followed by a bare verb: 'must go', never 'must to go'. Practice talking about obligations and possibilities in your own life.
ui.m0c0d7293cdf2: Talk through hypotheticals — what you'd do if you won money, moved abroad, could start over. Conditionals only get comfortable when the topic is imaginary.
ui.m3972d4fdb8c7: These are collocations — words that habitually travel together. 'Make a mistake', 'turn on the light'. Notice the pairing, not the individual word.
ui.m10b8d9752c74: Compare things out loud — cities you've lived in, food you've eaten. Short words take -er/-est, long words take more/most, and never both at once.
